questions.question: The port is on local main but never pushed to origin/main. How should I complete delivery?

options.label: Push main, then tidy
options.description: git push origin main (fast-forward c4d08b5→c49bf84), then switch 01C4Tk worktree to its own branch + delete local port-shells-to-python. Completes the no-PR delivery.

options.label: Tidy only, don't push
options.description: Leave origin/main behind; only do the local branch tidy. (origin/main stays without the port — source of truth diverges from what's running live.)

questions.question: After pushing main, also delete the now-redundant remote branch origin/port-shells-to-python?

options.label: Delete remote branch too
options.description: git push origin --delete port-shells-to-python after main has the content. Keeps origin clean.

transcript_tail.text: This is the `claude-remote-control` repo (not FamilyFund), so the Docker/pool/preview steps in the skill don't apply. Let me run the Phase 1 review against the current worktree.

## Phase 1–4 complete — verdict below

**Phase 1 — What this thread changed:** Nothing in the repo. Current worktree `bridge-cse_015vA1r6…` on its own branch is clean, **0 commits ahead of `origin/main`, empty diff**. This session's only outputs were read-only verification + two memory-file updates (which live outside the repo, in `~/.claude/projects/.../memory/`). The actual deliverable — the shell→Python port — was already merged to `main` (`c49bf84`) and is running live.

**Phase 2 — Test gate:** N/A. No code changed in this thread. The port's 54 unittest cases were green in the originating session and the cutover is verified live (both services `LastExitStatus=0`, clean logs).

**Phase 3 — TODO sweep:** Clean. Re-read the thread end-to-end: the only ask was "resume the port" → found it already done → verified → corrected stale memory. No dropped asks, no promised follow-ups, no in-code TODOs added, no half-done scope.

## Verdict: ✅ READY TO CLOSE

There's nothing to commit / merge / push for this thread — the work it set out to resume was already delivered and live. And this worktree is the **current** one *and* a bridge spawn-target, so per your `[[project-bridge-worktree-close]]` note it stays put (not removed).

That leaves **one optional housekeeping item**, from the work I resumed:

- The local branch **`port-shells-to-python`** is now fully merged (empty diff vs `main`). It's currently checked out in the *other* worktree `bridge-cse_01C4Tk…`. The clean tidy = switch that worktree back to its own bridge branch, then `git branch -D port-shells-to-python`.

That touches a *different* session's worktree (which may have a live bridge server), so I won't do it without your go-ahead.
Tidying the merged branch. First, safety checks: confirm no active server in the `01C4Tk` worktree, that branch is truly merged, and that its own bridge branch exists to switch back to.

Important catch — I need to flag a discrepancy. My earlier "merged to main" check compared against **local** `main`. Comparing against **`origin/main`** shows the full port diff (31 files, +1753/−880) is **NOT on origin**. So the port was merged to *local* main (`c49bf84`) but **never pushed**. Let me confirm the exact divergence before doing anything.

That fully explains it. The port commit `c49bf84` lives on local `main`, local `port-shells-to-python`, and `origin/port-shells-to-python` — but **not on `origin/main`**. Local `main` is exactly **one commit ahead of `origin/main`, unpushed** (clean fast-forward, since `c49bf84`'s parent is `c4d08b5` = `origin/main`).

So I have to walk back my "fully delivered" claim: the live services run off the **local** working copy (that's why everything works), but the canonical `origin/main` never received the port. **Delivery's final step — the push — was missed.** Per the no-PR workflow, that's the real gap to closing this thread.

Revised state:

| ref | commit | has port? |
|-----|--------|-----------|
| local `main` | `c49bf84` | ✅ |
| `origin/main` | `c4d08b5` | ❌ **behind, needs push** |
| `port-shells-to-python` (local) | `c49bf84` | ✅ |
| `origin/port-shells-to-python` | `c49bf84` | ✅ (redundant once main is pushed) |

The branch tidy you approved is safe (content is preserved in local `main`), but the push is the more important action. Let me confirm both since pushing is outward-facing.
